issues.failure_explanation: For x in M, Cx lies in ker(AB) but need not lie in ker(B)^perp, so x -> Cx does not map M into L. Example: n=1, B=[1,0], C=[1;1], A=0 gives M=F, but Cx=(x,x) is not in ker(B)^perp=span(e1). The dimension comparison dim M <= dim L is therefore not justified as written.

failure_location.quote: Consider $\Matrix{x} \mapsto \Matrix{Cx}$ as an injective linear operator $\Linop{C} : \mathbb{M} \to \mathbb{L}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use x -> P Cx, with P the orthogonal projector onto ker(B)^perp. This maps M into L, since AB(Cx)=0 implies AB(PCx)=0. It is injective, since PCx=0 forces x in ker(BC) and hence x=0.
issues.overall_effect: Part 2 (Frobenius) is unsupported as written. Part 3 (Sylvester) and its uses in lemma:rank_properties inherit the gap, but all statements remain true.
issues.title: Frobenius inequality proof uses an ill-defined map M -> L
issues.why_classification: A short local fix restores the argument with no loss of content.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Note that $\Matrix{B}^\pinv \Matrix{B} = \Matrix{I}_{m}$ and $\Matrix{C} \Matrix{C}^\pinv = \Matrix{I}_{n}$, then substitute $\Matrix{C}^\pinv \Batrix{A}^\pinv \Matrix{B}^\pinv$ into Theorem~\ref{theorem:pinv_bochner}.

issues.failure_explanation: Substitution gives (BAC)(C^+A^+B^+) = B AA^+ B^+, which is not self-adjoint unless B^+ = B^*; similarly for the other Hermitian condition. So two Penrose conditions fail. Counterexample with H=F: A=[1,0], B=[1], C=[[1,0],[1,1]]. Then (AC)^+=[1;0], while C^{-1}A^+=[1;-1].

failure_location.quote: If $\Matrix{B} \in \F^{k \times m}$ has full column rank and $\Matrix{C} \in \F^{n \times l}$ has full row rank, $(\Matrix{B} \Batrix{A} \Matrix{C})^\pinv = \Matrix{C}^\pinv \Batrix{A}^\pinv \Matrix{B}^\pinv$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict part 2 to B with orthonormal columns and C with orthonormal rows, where B^+=B^* and C^+=C^* make the substitution valid. Alternatively, replace it by the full-rank-factorization rule (FG)^+=G^+F^+ for F of full column rank and G of full row rank, with proof.
issues.overall_effect: Part 2 of lem:added-8 is false as stated. No labelled result cites it; lemma:cur_column uses a different, true full-rank-factorization rule.
issues.title: False reverse-order law for pseudoinverse with full-rank (non-orthonormal) factors
issues.why_classification: The stated generality is false. The fix necessarily weakens or replaces the claim, but a comparable result survives and nothing depends on it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In our experiment, we choose $\alpha_{\max} = \beta_{\max} = 2$, $m = n = 100$, and $K = 75$.

issues.failure_explanation: A sine expansion of -u''-α²u=cos(βx) gives (k²-α²)u_k = (2/π)·k[1-(-1)^k cos βπ]/(k²-β²). Thus both denominators in the stated u_k have the wrong sign. Moreover, k²=α² at α=1,2, and α=2 is a grid point. There the BVP has no solution, since the sin(2x) coefficient 1-cos(βπ) is generically nonzero. So the claimed solution map on [0,2]² does not exist, and the computed matrix is not the solution map of eq:ode_bvp.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either restate a well-posed problem (e.g., -u''+α²u with matching right-hand side coefficients) whose sine coefficients are exactly the ones used, or recompute u_k for a well-posed version of eq:ode_bvp and rerun the experiment.
issues.overall_effect: The first experiment does not approximate the solution map of the stated problem. Its conclusions about that PDE map (Figure 1) refer to a different, unspecified parametric function.
issues.title: Stated series is not the solution of the stated BVP, which is singular on the grid
issues.why_classification: There is no single forced correction. Either the problem must be redefined or the experiment rerun, but the method and the other results are unaffected.
